how_to_read.note: LLM: this file can be large - do NOT read it whole. Look up ONLY the key you need; most answers are a few lines.
how_to_read.configure_an_IP: 1) ip_index['<ip>'] (schematic-resolved, e.g. enet0/lpuart2) for pins+coverage. 2) if the IP is not there, find candidate balls by scanning soc_pins for ones whose mux_options names the function (e.g. 'LPUART3_TX'); prefer balls with empty behind_hw_mux/on_connector. 3) read the chosen balls in soc_pins['<ball>']. (Regenerate with --candidates for a pre-built ip_candidates['<instance>'] menu, omitted by default to keep the file lean.)
how_to_read.what_can_this_ball_be: soc_pins['<ball>'].mux_options = space-separated function names (full macro = IOMUXC_<ball>_<func> on IOMUXC boards).
how_to_read.ask_the_user: needs_verification[] = conflicts + ambiguous instance/mux choices the netlist cannot decide.
how_to_read.tell_the_user: hw_muxes[] + soc_pins[].behind_hw_mux = on-board mux/jumper workarounds; honor electrical.external_pull when setting pad bias.
how_to_read.trust: resolved pins are a high-confidence DRAFT - verify clock/boot/console by build/run. Full contract in 'consumption'.

about.purpose: netlist + SoC mux header -> agent-readable pin facts for NPI Zephyr/SDK enablement
about.consume: query by IP via ip_index; or read whole. soc_pins is the pin-keyed ground truth.

sections.soc_pins: every SoC ball: net, status(resolved/needs-review/unresolved/unconnected), mux_options (compact list of function names the ball can be; macro=IOMUXC_<ball>_<func>), behind_hw_mux, on_connector
sections.ip_index: per-IP (as epics name them, e.g. enet0/lpuart2): pins, recommended instance, caveats, coverage=full|partial|needs-human — RESOLVED IPs only
sections.ip_candidates: per-instance CAPABILITY x FEASIBILITY menu for ANY IP (lpuart3/lpi2c1/flexcan1/gpt1/...): candidate balls + placement(free/header/behind-hw-mux/taken). Pick a usable instance even when the schematic didn't resolve it; then honour the tell(hw_muxes)/ask(needs_verification) split
sections.gpio: recognized LED/button nets resolved to GPIO port/pin + mux macro (SDK BOARD_InitLEDs/Buttons; Zephyr gpio-leds/gpio-keys)
sections.peripherals: resolved peripheral pins with mux_macro + per-pin usage (detail)
sections.connectors: expansion/functional connectors: full mux options per pin + reuse class + layout cross-check
sections.hw_muxes: on-board signal muxes (mux-ic / resistor-jumper / jumper-cap / jumper-selectable): routes + control; default side NOT in netlist
sections.needs_review: pins the matcher refuses to guess (signal conflict / ambiguous) — human or KB needed

about.honesty: mux default sides, connector physical intent, and multi-instance disambiguation are often NOT in the netlist; those fields are null/needs-human, never guessed. Output is format-neutral facts; SDK IOMUXC_* macros are one rendering.

consumption._: How a downstream workflow should consume this file as the board's pin-config source of truth.
consumption.entry_point: To CONFIGURE an IP: first try ip_index[<ip>] (schematic-resolved, high-confidence). If the IP is not there (net-name-poor board), use ip_candidates[<instance>] to pick A usable instance from the capability x feasibility menu (prefer placement=free/header over behind-hw-mux/taken), read the chosen balls' full mux_options in soc_pins, then TELL the user any hw_muxes/behind_hw_mux workaround and ASK about matching needs_verification items.

coverage_gating.full: all pins resolved and ready -> safe to auto-generate this IP's pin config
coverage_gating.partial: resolved, but some pins need a jumper / board-mux / external wiring (see caveats) -> auto-generate AND surface the caveats
coverage_gating.needs-human: signal conflict or multi-instance ambiguity -> STOP, route to a human/RM (details in needs_review)

consumption.never_guess: Fields that are null or 'needs-human' are NOT in the netlist and must not be inferred: hw_muxes[].default_route, jumper-selectable routes, connector intent, and any pin whose net is ball-named (e.g. PIO0_6) or auto-named (Nxxxx).
consumption.trust: Resolved pins are a HIGH-CONFIDENCE DRAFT (~94% IOMUXC / ~88% IOPCTL on validated boards), not a guarantee. Verify runtime-critical pins (clock/boot/debug console) by build/run before relying on them.
consumption.rendering: Format-neutral facts. SDK: emit IOMUXC_SetPinMux from peripherals[].mux_macro + BOARD_InitLEDs/Buttons from gpio[]. Zephyr: pinmux=<&...> from the same ball+function + gpio-leds/gpio-keys from gpio[] port/pin.
consumption.pad_config: When generating a pin's pad/bias config, HONOR its electrical{} (present on peripherals[] and needs_review[]): if external_pull is set, the board already pulls the line -> set bias-disable / leave the internal pull OFF (enabling it would halve the board pull and shift I2C levels/edges). open_drain:true marks I2C/I3C lines. drive_strength/slew_rate are application-dependent (tool does not set them).
consumption.completeness_note: coverage tracks how functionally the schematic names its nets; a board with ball-named nets yields many needs-human pins (not a tool error).
consumption.verify_loop: needs_verification[] lists every item the netlist can't decide, each with a human-facing question + the overlay key to record the answer. Flow: agent reads needs_verification -> asks the human -> writes answers to a verify overlay (yaml: pins/hw_muxes) -> regenerate with --verify. The answers are baked back in and stamped verification:human-confirmed (provenance.verify_overlay records the file). A field marked human-confirmed is no longer a draft — trust it.

provenance.note: RM rev not in mux header; trust soc_mux.sha256_16 fingerprint.
